description: M6 physics gate tolerances, expected per-engine deviations and allowed skips (docs/03_WorkPlan.md M6, docs/02_Architecture.md 14.3, DL23). Every default is the 03 criterion or names the physics it bounds; every override and every allowed skip names the engine behaviour that causes it. 03 M6 asks for registration BEFORE the run: entries marked "registered": "post-run" were found on a run and registered only after their mechanism was verified in the engine source (docs/Progress.md M6 D-3, D-4, D-6); each carries "sign_off": "pending" until the lead accepts it, then who accepted it and when (the loader refuses a post-run entry without one). A gate never widens a value by itself, and an unregistered Skip is a Fail (Gates/PhysicsGates.h). Its SHA-256 goes into conformance.json (and into the M10 stamp, DL20).

overrides.reason: PhysX PGS creep (measured M6, Progress D-4; 03 says mu 0.6 holds, so this needs the lead's acceptance): the mu 0.6 box does not accelerate (hold_acceleration_cms2 holds) but creeps down the 30 deg slope at a constant ~2.5 cm/s and never stops in Normalized (0.73 cm by frame 20, 4.6 cm by frame 120; bounded by hold_speed_cms). It is a property of PGS patch friction near the friction limit, not of the backend or of UE4's single velocity iteration. A raw PhysX 5.11 program with no harness and no adapter (the M6 checker's rawpx_incline: the same 50 cm / 10 kg cube, UE4-style scene in cm, tolerances 100 / 1000, PGS 8 / 1, PCM, contact offset 2, sleep off; Progress M6 section 8) reproduces it to within 0.01 cm: 0.7322 cm at frame 20, 4.6304 cm at frame 120, 2.504 / 2.478 cm/s; PGS 4 / 1 the same; mu 0.65 1.05 / 0.95 cm/s, mu 0.70 0.39 cm/s (about 0.2-0.4 cm/s at mu 0.7 depending on the setup), mu 0.75 and 0.80 hold; TGS 0.07 cm/s. Through the harness (Progress M6 section 7, Normalized, frame 20 / creep): 4 velocity iterations 0.32 cm / 0.93-1.05 cm/s, 32 position iterations 0.73 cm / 2.3-2.5 cm/s (no change), PxSceneFlag::eENABLE_FRICTION_EVERY_ITERATION 0.14 cm / 0.45 cm/s (still creeping, and UE4 did not set it); TGS, Jolt and Bullet hold (<= 0.05 cm). The SDK documents it: PGS processes the two friction axes separately, which 'can lead to asymmetries when transitioning from dynamic to static friction', and applies friction in the last 3 position iterations and the velocity iterations only (PxSceneDesc.h:34-42, :245-259 [V])

G9.description: Every READBACK key of the M3.BoxPile 1k effective dump must match one rule here (M7: the bench preflight applies the same rules to the effective dump of the run's own scene; a rule with "scene" holds for that scene's geometry only and is skipped, with a note, on another scene): compared with its resolved value (profile:, option:, init:, capacity:, const:, min:, text rules) or registered as 'unchecked' with the reason it has no resolved counterpart. A key whose backend checks each engine object against the host's rule reads back canonical = the number of objects that do NOT hold it (docs/Abi.md 5.14), compared with const:0. Rule lookup: '<Engine>.<Variant>', then '<Engine>', then '*'. An unregistered READBACK key fails G9.
